verdict: Hot stuff, Marks — this one cooks. The Arabian-Nights-as-wrestling-territory frame is a knockout pitch and almost every persona lands as 'someone you can be at the table.' Strength: the SoD meter and named tropes (Pink Slip, Reluctant Three-Count, Cheap Heat) turn jokes into mechanics. Weakness: the Three-Apples and field-hazard cards lean observational and could use a louder do-this-now hook. Table-ready Y.
blurb: A stand-alone expansion that retells One Thousand and One Nights as a wrestling territory. For players who already love Kayfabizarro and want a story arc with Heels, Faces, and a Pink Slip on the line.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — Bazaar skyline with rabbit MC is rich, evocative, slightly busy
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — '1001 Kayfabe Nights' is the whole pitch in three words
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Mashup is fresh inside the catalog, archetypal outside
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Title alone is shareable; deck-with-Pink-Slip premise has hook
coverQA.coverNote: FrizzleBob says: cover earns the click. Title carries it, art seals the bazaar promise. Tighten the figure hierarchy and this one's a tentpole cover for the series.

notes: Layout is 2x2 landscape, 4 cards per page. Page 1 is cover + 3 framework cards (Manifesto, Rules: The Meter, Warning). Pages 2-15 are themed acts: Royal Court, Aladdin, Sinbad Vol 1/2, Ali Baba Cave, 39 Thieves, City of Brass Automata, City of Brass Ghost Town, Ebony Horse, Low Card Comedy, Blame Game, Commission Legends, Three Apples Noir, Meta-Tools. RAF dice present on every card. Wrestling vocabulary (push, heel, face, heat, pop, sell, shoot, work, screwjob, kayfabe, valet, jobber) used throughout with discipline. No visible font artifacts. Sub-deck arc structure is the cleverest move — each page tells a mini-storyline.

quickWins: Add a one-liner suggesting which sub-arc to start with in the Manifesto card
Promote 'Stay Fluffy' as a verbal kayfabe call-and-response in the Rules card
niceToHave: A back-cover sub-arc index would help on Gumroad listing
Three Apples sub-arc could use one more performative card to balance the cluescape

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: 1001 KAYFABE NIGHTS – Tell a Better Story or Take the Pink Slip (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

One weak story and the sultan has you gone by sunrise. Scheherazade booked herself a thousand-night title run instead.

That is the engine of the original Nights: a storyteller performing for her life, cutting every tale on a cliffhanger so the morning never arrives. This deck takes that premise at its word and racks it as a wrestling territory, with heels, faces, heat, and a Pink Slip on the line every round. The Royal Court wants you written off the card by dawn. Your only counter is the next story, and it had better pop.

1001 Kayfabe Nights is Social Story Wrestling booked as a fourteen-act territory. You draw a card, perform the tale out loud, and the table rules whether it carries the night or sends you to the back. It runs stand-alone, and it runs hotter for anyone already living in the Kayfabizarro Kosmos.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The 1001 Nights Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards across fourteen themed acts, featuring SHAHRYĀR, THE DESTROYER, the sultan booking executions until a better story talks him down, ABU HASAN, whose one humiliating mistake follows him across an entire act while the room refuses to let it die, and THE BARBER, the talker who can stall any court to death with a story that will not end.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, the RAF dice riding every card, and The Meter, the rule that clocks your tale and calls the night the moment the table stops buying it.
- The Territory Engine: fourteen acts racked back to back, from the Royal Court and the Ali Baba Cave to the City of Brass automata and Three Apples Noir, each page a self-contained storyline you can run cold or chain into one long thousand-night arc.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This deck rides the Komik Kard Kult line. Grab it and you are not buying a frozen PDF, you are on the pipeline: every future act, booster, and bedtime brawl in this cycle reaches you as a free update, no second checkout.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because the oldest survival skill we have is being worth listening to one more night, and nobody teaches it as a contact sport. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, deal it, talk your way out of a corner. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the rules.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The story never had to be true. It only had to last until morning."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
